away.name: Justus Annunen

home.name: Laurent Brossoit
home.news: Brossoit returned last season after nearly two years out with an injury and has mostly played in the AHL since, but is currently getting a look in the Ducks' crease. Amid struggles from Lukas Dostal and Ville Husso, Brossoit will tend the twine for the fourth time in five games. The 33-year-old Brossoit has been far from spectacular, posting a 3.26 GAA and .877 SV%, but remains undefeated at 4-0-0. He is coming off his best outing so far, saving 31 of 33 shots (.939 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Ducks enter Wednesday's game as -136 home favourites against a Nashville Predators team that played last night and defeated the Los Angeles Kings 3-0.

away.name: Sergei Murashov
away.news: The Penguins have struggled this season, and goaltending has rarely helped them, whether it's Arturs Silovs or Sergei Murashov. The 22-year-old Murashov has seen limited action this season and has faced adversity, but he's coming off a solid outing, saving 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the Los Angeles Kings. That said, he has allowed four or more goals in three of his last four games (1-3-0). The Penguins enter Wednesday's contest as -137 road favourites against a San Jose Sharks team that has scored two or fewer goals in five of their last six games (1-5-0).

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov has had an up-and-down 2026-27 season. After one of the best stretches of his career at the NHL level, Askarov allowed 11 goals on 54 shots in two games (0-2-0), but rebounded in his most recent outing, saving 30 of 32 shots (.938 SV%) in a 3-2 shootout win over the New York Islanders. The 24-year-old goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in six of his last eight games (3-5-0). The Sharks enter Monday's outing as +124 home underdogs against a Pittsburgh Penguins team coming off a 5-2 loss to the Anaheim Ducks.
